questions.question: What does a static field represent?

options.value: One class-level variable shared by its instances
A separate copy in every object
A parameter local to one call

questions.explanation: static describes association with the class, not immutability.

questions.question: What does an instance field represent?

options.value: Exactly one value for the entire class

questions.explanation: Each object has its own instance-field storage.

questions.question: Can a static method directly use this?
questions.explanation: A static method has no particular receiver object.

questions.question: Can a static method access an instance field through an explicit object reference?

options.value: Only if the field is final
Only when the reference is null

questions.explanation: An explicit receiver identifies which object’s state is being accessed.

questions.question: Which is conventional syntax for a static method call?
questions.explanation: The class name communicates that the call is class-level.

questions.question: Does static alone make a field constant?
questions.explanation: final, not static, restricts reassignment after initialization.

questions.question: When an instance method changes a static field, who observes that shared value?

options.value: Other code accessing the same class field

questions.explanation: The field has one shared class-level value.

questions.question: What is a typical use for a static field?

options.value: A separate name for each player
A separate balance for each account
A local subtotal for one invocation
A count of objects created by the class

questions.explanation: A class-wide count should be shared rather than duplicated per object.

questions.question: A class field static int created starts at 0. Each constructor increments it once. What is created after 2 new objects?
questions.explanation: Every constructor call updates the same shared counter.

questions.question: Counter has static int total = 0 and per-object int count = 0. One object increments its count 2 times. A second untouched object has what count?
questions.explanation: Updating one instance field does not change the other instance’s field.
